Check the balance of a split or of a set of resamples

Source: R/balance_check.R
balance_check.Rd

balance_check() compares the assessment set of each split with its analysis set. For a three-way split, it compares the validation set and the testing set each with the training set. It reports a standardized mean difference (SMD) for each variable and the energy distance for all variables together. It works with any rset or rsplit, so you can compare balanced folds with ordinary rsample::vfold_cv() folds.

Usage

balance_check(x, ..., max_n = 2000)

# S3 method for class 'rset'
balance_check(x, ..., max_n = 2000)

# S3 method for class 'rsplit'
balance_check(x, ..., max_n = 2000)

# S3 method for class 'three_way_split'
balance_check(x, ..., max_n = 2000)

# S3 method for class 'balance_check'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

An rset (for example from balanced_vfold_cv()), an rsplit (for example from balanced_initial_split()), or a three-way split (from balanced_initial_validation_split() or rsample::initial_validation_split()).

...

For balance_check(), <tidy-select> columns to check. If empty, the balance and exact columns stored in x are used. For summary(), not used and must be empty.

max_n

The largest number of rows per set for the energy distance. Larger sets are subsampled at random to keep memory use low.

object

A balance_check object.

Value

A tibble with class balance_check. It has the ID columns of x, and the columns variable, level, statistic ("smd" or "energy"), and value. Energy rows have NA in variable and level.

summary() returns a tibble with one row per split. It has the ID columns, max_abs_smd (the largest absolute SMD in the split), the variable and level with that SMD (the first one if several tie), and energy. If the split has no SMD that isn't missing, max_abs_smd, variable, and level are NA. If it has no energy row, energy is NA. Each split must have its own ID, so no ID may have more than one energy row. Only the ID columns that balance_check() made are used, so columns you add are ignored. If you rename or drop an ID column, the columns whose names start with id are used instead.

Details

For a numeric variable, the SMD is the difference in means (assessment minus analysis) divided by the pooled standard deviation, sqrt((var_assessment + var_analysis) / 2). For a categorical variable, there is one SMD per level, from the proportions of that level. Values under 0.1 in absolute size are often taken as good balance. If both sets have zero variance but different means, the SMD is Inf or -Inf; the plot shows these values at the edge of the panel.

Missing values are dropped variable by variable for the SMD. The energy distance uses the rows that have no missing values in any checked column.

The energy distance is the V-statistic 2 E|X - Y| - E|X - X'| - E|Y - Y'| on the standardized variables (one indicator column per categorical level). It is 0 when the two sets have the same distribution, and it also detects differences in spread and shape.

Use summary() on the result to get one row per split.

Examples

set.seed(1)
folds <- balanced_vfold_cv(mtcars, v = 4, balance = c(mpg, hp, wt))
balance_check(folds)
#> # Balance check: 4 splits, max |SMD| = 0.138, mean energy distance = 0.133
#> # A tibble: 16 × 5
#>    id    variable level statistic     value
#>    <chr> <chr>    <chr> <chr>         <dbl>
#>  1 Fold1 mpg      NA    smd       -0.0998  
#>  2 Fold1 hp       NA    smd        0.109   
#>  3 Fold1 wt       NA    smd       -0.138   
#>  4 Fold1 NA       NA    energy     0.212   
#>  5 Fold2 mpg      NA    smd        0.0759  
#>  6 Fold2 hp       NA    smd        0.00594 
#>  7 Fold2 wt       NA    smd        0.0691  
#>  8 Fold2 NA       NA    energy     0.118   
#>  9 Fold3 mpg      NA    smd        0.0154  
#> 10 Fold3 hp       NA    smd       -0.0498  
#> 11 Fold3 wt       NA    smd        0.0603  
#> 12 Fold3 NA       NA    energy     0.0961  
#> 13 Fold4 mpg      NA    smd        0.00471 
#> 14 Fold4 hp       NA    smd       -0.0734  
#> 15 Fold4 wt       NA    smd        0.000164
#> 16 Fold4 NA       NA    energy     0.105   
summary(balance_check(folds))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   id    max_abs_smd variable level energy
#>   <chr>       <dbl> <chr>    <chr>  <dbl>
#> 1 Fold1      0.138  wt       NA    0.212 
#> 2 Fold2      0.0759 mpg      NA    0.118 
#> 3 Fold3      0.0603 wt       NA    0.0961
#> 4 Fold4      0.0734 hp       NA    0.105 

# Compare with ordinary folds
summary(balance_check(rsample::vfold_cv(mtcars, v = 4), mpg, hp, wt))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   id    max_abs_smd variable level energy
#>   <chr>       <dbl> <chr>    <chr>  <dbl>
#> 1 Fold1       0.518 hp       NA     0.401
#> 2 Fold2       0.904 hp       NA     0.687
#> 3 Fold3       0.510 wt       NA     0.291
#> 4 Fold4       0.232 hp       NA     0.333
